newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI sees higher profit in '96/97 - chief.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI sees higher profit in '96/97 - chief.

text.p: State Bank of India (SBI) will post an impressive increase in net profit in 1996/97 (April-March), its chairman said on Monday.

"On the basis of coupon rates, the government has fixed a range between 13.62 to 13.68 percent, we will be able to report a substantial increase in profit," P.G. Kakodkar told Reuters in the eastern city of Bhubaneswar.
He did not give any further details.
SBI, India's largest commercial bank, reported a net profit of 8.32 billion rupees ($234 million) in 1995/96 compared to 7.15 billion in the previous year.

"Had it not been for the increase in the coupon rates announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Yield to Maturity (YTM) at 14 percent, we would have made much more profit (in 1995/96)," Kakodkar said.
